description:
Today `inline/4` in lib/defk/compiler.ex binds every array argument of an inlined callee with owned: false, so `h[i] = v` inside a helper kernel is rejected with read-only-array even when the caller created h with alloc/2. Any text kernel wants `insert(table, keys, stats, name_start, name_len, temp)` as a helper; without this, the whole hash table update has to be written inline in the one kernel body, and so does every other array-mutating helper.

Options:
(a) Pass ownership through inlining: an argument whose value is owned stays owned in the callee (it is the same C variable after aliasing). Simple, and since the callee is inlined the write happens in the caller's frame anyway. Elixir mode already threads written arrays out of blocks; a callee writing a parameter needs the same threading across the call: the Elixir-mode call returns the written arrays alongside its result (Ops-level tuple), which value semantics (defk-auo) requires anyway.
(b) An explicit marker in the head, e.g. `insert(h :: mut [i64], ...)`, so the signature says which parameters are written. More visible, and gives the Elixir-mode emitter the list of threaded arrays without inspecting the body.

Recommendation: (b), because it keeps the "a write gives that variable a new array" story readable at the call site (`h = insert(h, ...)` is still how Elixir mode sees it) and because defk-auo will need the list. Decide with defk-auo's owner; that is why this is needs-triage.

Done when: a helper kernel can write to a mut array parameter, the write is visible to the caller after the call in both modes, writes to a non-mut parameter are still rejected with a clear error and rewrite, and resume tests cover a helper writing inside a yielding loop.

comments.text: Decision update after reading defk-dtw.18: drop option (b), the mut marker. The project already decided that a write to a parameter array that is never returned is a compile error, so the construct is: an inlined helper may write to a parameter array only if it returns that array (alone or in a tuple), and the caller rebinds it: `{slots, arena, stats, n} = insert(slots, arena, stats, ...)`. Compiler: in inline/4, a parameter bound to an owned argument stays owned when the callee returns it (return-input-array no longer applies to an owned argument); a write to a parameter that is not returned raises the dtw.18 error with the rewrite. Elixir mode needs no new threading: the callee returns the new binary as any value. This keeps the one rule: Elixir value semantics, no in-place mutation visible through another name. Relabel ready-for-agent once defk-auo confirms copy-on-aliased-write does not change the owned-argument rule.

title: Helper kernels can write to arrays their caller allocated
